newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sydney shoppers hurt by toxic fumes.
newsitem.headline: Sydney shoppers hurt by toxic fumes.

text.p: Twelve people were taken to hospital and 500 evacuated from a Sydney supermarket on Friday after an unexploded liquid chlorine bomb gave off toxic fumes.
Police said it was the second chlorine bomb found in a city supermarket this week, but they did not know whether the two devices were linked.
Friday's bomb, in a container the size of a small bucket, was discovered inside a supermarket at Bondi Junction in Sydney's eastern suburbs at around 11.00 a.m. (2400GMT).
"It was giving off chlorine fumes, but it did not explode," fire brigade spokesman Paul Rafferty told Reuters. Police said earlier the device had exploded.
Fire brigade officers placed the bomb in a drum of water to stop it going off, allowing the police bomb squad to later defused it.
The bomb was a liquid mixture containing chlorine which would have exploded if left unattended, said fire brigade officer Peter Status.
"This particular device was not designed to cause a great explosion, but it is still a worry to us. The chemical reaction would eventually have caused an explosion," Status said.
"Police are investigating the device to determine whether it was a nuisance device or whether it was set to deliberately injure people," he said.
Ambulance officials said 12 people had been taken to hospital suffering from the effects of chlorine inhalation, while 500 other shoppers and staff had been evacuated.
The shopping centre's air-conditioning system was used to remove toxic fumes from the building.
A similar liquid chlorine bomb was found by cleaners in a garbage bin in a supermarket in the nearby suburb of Randwick on Wednesday, police said.

"The cleaners discovered that device in the supermarket and took it out to the car park. It was giving off fumes, which got into the supermarket's air conditioning system," a Randwick police spokesman told Reuters.
Police said only a few people were affected by the toxic fumes, but the Randwick building also had to be evacuated.
